intent: Independently assess the proposed bounded transfer-analysis transport recovery before source edits.
latency_counting: Deduplicated complete call objects across each directory's354 logical generation rows, eliminating six alias rows. Each recovered directory describes its retained/latest evidence, not a cumulative count of all historical attempts.
recommendation: Use60seconds rather than lengthening each attempt: recovered successful-call p99 is50.957seconds; two60second attempts leave nominal30seconds under the observed150second platform limit. The one164.376second success would already exceed that limit. Observed latency is support for this bounded choice, not a guarantee of future completion.
required_implementation_boundaries: Construct the serialized target request once and reuse identical bytes for the second transport attempt. Keep target-level retries inside the existing parallel item processing; a completed valid sibling is not requested again within that invocation.
Apply the timeout through fetch AND full body acquisition. A timer cleared immediately after headers would leave the observed body-read hang unbounded.

Separate body acquisition from JSON/model-output validation. Network/body-read abort may retry; completed HTTP200 invalid JSON, invalid envelope, length finish_reason, schema-invalid output and semantic/state/type rejection must not retry.
Retry only the named transient HTTP statuses; other HTTP errors terminate this invocation. Consume or cancel failed response bodies and clear each attempt timer.
Keep apply_transfer_message_analysis_v1 after all target validations. An exhausted or invalid target must not partially apply other targets.

Do not claim a hard150second bound for prepare_turn: it awaits analysis then starts separate assessment generation and possible format repair. Its sequential path needs remaining-time handling or a separately scoped verification/claim.

Promise.all rejection does not cancel sibling promises. Ensure terminal operation failure does not launch further unnecessary retry attempts; account for already in-flight requests and unknown provider completion after client abort.
focused_handler_verification: Two target items: one succeeds once; the other transport-fails then succeeds. Assert1+2calls, identical retried bytes/settings and one complete final DBapply.
Hanging response body after HTTP200headers: attempt is aborted at the deadline and receives exactly one retry.
Completed HTTP200 malformed outer JSON, malformed model JSON, truncated model output and invalid event each produce the existing error without transport retry or DBapply.
Eligible429/502/503/504 each recover on the bounded second attempt; noneligible HTTP statuses never retry.
Two transport failures exhaust the item, return AI_PROVIDER_ERROR and never apply any target. Timers are cleared; valid siblings are not resampled.
Exercise prepare_turn when analysis was needed in the same invocation; verify the deadline interpretation rather than assuming analysis timeout alone bounds assessment generation.
limitations: Provider abort can leave an unknown server-side outcome; it does not prove the provider stopped computation.

With no durable cache, retained sibling successes live only within one invocation. A later client invocation after terminal failure may recompute those targets; do not describe this proposal as cross-request replay.

The transport change is a declared operational change to production delivery. It does not alter selected prompt/decoding settings, replace saved evaluation outcomes or convert benchmark failure to acceptance.
